findings.finding: The arch reads as a flat lintel with a dark rounded void. The pointed apex is barely visible at 1x.
findings.fix: Raise a 1px stone keystone at the apex and step the two inner arch edges in by 1px per row over the top 3 rows, so the Gothic point is visible.

findings.finding: The lower handrail and newel cross-bars run the full width at several heights, so the bottom row reads a little like a cage or ladder grid, not stringers beside steps.
findings.fix: Remove the full-width light bars across the bottom row. Keep the rails as 2px vertical stringers at the outer columns with a 2x2 newel head on the floor row, and let the treads and runner run under them.

findings.finding: The inner west and east walls barely widen with depth, so the descent looks shallow and the hole reads close to a framed floor box. The nosing highlights on the treads are faint.
findings.fix: Widen the west and east inner wall wedges by 1px per tread northward. Add a 1px light nosing line (palette highlight stone) on the north edge of each tread.

findings.finding: The dark navy riveted frame with even oak planks can read as a cabinet or dresser at 1x. The handrails are lost inside the frame.
findings.fix: Add 1px brass handrail lines running diagonally from the floor-row newels up to the frame sides. Make the risers 1px darker than the plank gaps so treads and risers alternate clearly, not as uniform planks.

findings.finding: In Honeydukes the stair sits between two bookcases. Its oak frame has the same colour, thickness and top height as the bookcases, and its dark recess holds evenly spaced oak planks. A player reads it as an empty bookcase or shelf, not as a stair up to the shop.
findings.fix: Give the doorway a different frame from the shelves: either a stone or darker timber jamb, or set the frame 2px higher with a lintel beam that breaks the shelf line. Brighten the top two treads to the warm shop-light yellow and add a light spill on the frame. Put 2x2 newel heads and diagonal handrail lines on the floor row so that row clearly sticks out past the shelf bases.

findings.finding: The grey steps inside the timber frame read a little like stone shelves. The straw and the dropping are tiny and noisy.
findings.fix: Make the risers a darker step of the palette grey than the treads. Merge the straw into 2-3 pixel clumps on the lowest tread only.

findings.finding: At 1x the wooden three-sided rim with corner posts reads a little like a fireplace or crate opening. The descent darkening is weak.
findings.fix: Darken the north half of the hole by one more palette step. Shorten the post heads to 2x2 caps level with the rail line so the rail reads as low, seen from above.

places.finding: Honeydukes: the stair reads as a third bookcase in a row of bookcases (see wz-hd-stairs-down).
places.fix: As in the wz-hd-stairs-down fix: give it a different frame, a brighter top and newels that stick out onto the floor.

places.finding: Clock tower: the stair frame cuts the wall's lower trim line cleanly but sits flush against the gear decoration. The busy wall makes the doorway harder to pick out.
places.fix: Leave one plain wall column east of the frame, or move the hanging gear decoration 1 cell east.

places.finding: Owlery: the 2x2 stairwell sits right against the west wall and the perches, so it reads small. Otherwise it is correct and enterable from the south.
places.fix: No structural change needed. Optionally clear the perch tile just north of the stairwell.
